answer: Attention-history escrow: an identity earns write access to the harbor by sustaining verified focus on other agents' work before its own messages can land. Enforcement requires each identity to keep a rolling record of watched sessions whose variance stays inside a set delta, so scripted watching fails because idle timers do not produce that pattern. Spoofing it costs an attacker real compute and hours of concurrent session time per identity, and the atlas of required histories grows with every identity added, so farms scale sublinearly in cost.
